precincts.name: Port Approach
precincts.role: Approach control and sensors for the port docks and the Hall of Arrivals
precincts.intro: 5,435 × 9,262 ft (1.66 × 2.82 km). Controllers who bring every ship into the port docks and the Hall of Arrivals.

buildings.name: Port Approach Control
buildings.notes: controllers for the port docks and the Hall of Arrivals
buildings.purpose: The approach control room for the port side. Controllers here guide every ship and shuttle coming in to the port docks and the Hall of Arrivals.
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with a long-span steel roof over the control room; raised floors for cables; blast-resistant glazing.
buildings.look: A long low control block in dark graphite with a band of blue-lit screens visible through tall tinted windows, and radio masts along its roof.
buildings.entrances: Staff entrance with security gate; equipment door at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 40 controller desks; 4,930 staff over three watches.
buildings.services: Duplicate power feeds, battery back-up, dual data links to the Traffic Control Centre and the Beacon.
buildings.interior: Equipment floor (L1): Port approach control room, light court, equipment room, uninterruptible power room, engineers' workshop, entrance and security, locker room, staff toilets and showers, arrivals liaison desk. Control floor (L2): Port approach control room, flow management desk, watch manager's office, quiet room, tea point, assistants' room. Support floor (L3): Briefing room, training simulator room, rest lounge, records and tapes room, staff toilets and showers, offices.

buildings.name: Port Sensor Hall

buildings.structure: Steel portal-frame hall with screened walls to stop radio leaks; concrete support wing.
buildings.look: A tall windowless hall in ribbed dark metal, crowned with radomes and cable masts, with yellow service doors.
buildings.entrances: Equipment doors big enough for a truck; staff door by the control room.
buildings.capacity: Radar and sensor coverage of the port approaches; a crew of about 20 per shift.
buildings.services: Radio-screened walls, chilled water, duplicate power.
buildings.interior: Array floor (L1): Radar bay 1, radar bay 2, radar bay 3, radar bay 4, radar bay 5, radar bay 6, radar bay 7, radar bay 8, radar bay 9 and 8 more rooms. buildings.name: Pilot Boat Station

buildings.capacity: A fleet of pilot boats; 800 crew.

precincts.name: Starboard Approach
precincts.role: Approach control for the Cruiser Gates, rescue coordination, evacuation craft
precincts.intro: 5,435 × 9,262 ft (1.66 × 2.82 km). Approach control for the three Cruiser Gates and the starboard side, and the rescue centre.

buildings.name: Starboard Approach Control
buildings.notes: controllers for the Cruiser Gates and the starboard side
buildings.purpose: The approach control room for the starboard side. Controllers here guide cruisers through the three Cruiser Gates.
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with a long-span steel roof over the control room; raised floors for cables; blast-resistant glazing.
buildings.look: A long low control block in dark graphite with a band of blue-lit screens visible through tall tinted windows, and radio masts along its roof.
buildings.entrances: Staff entrance with security gate; equipment door at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 40 controller desks; 12,340 staff over three watches.
buildings.services: Duplicate power feeds, battery back-up, dual data links to the Traffic Control Centre and the Beacon.
buildings.interior: Equipment floor (L1): Starboard approach control room, equipment room, uninterruptible power room, engineers' workshop, entrance and security, locker room, staff toilets and showers, gate liaison desk. Control floor (L2): Starboard approach control room, flow management desk, watch manager's office, quiet room, tea point, cruiser movement desk, assistants' room. Support floor 1 to Support floor 2 (L3–L4): Briefing room, training simulator room, rest lounge, records and tapes room, staff toilets and showers, offices.

buildings.name: Starboard Sensor Hall
buildings.notes: radar and sensor arrays for the starboard approaches
buildings.purpose: The radar and sensor hall tracking every craft approaching the starboard side of the ship.
buildings.structure: Steel portal-frame hall with screened walls to stop radio leaks; concrete support wing.
buildings.look: A tall windowless hall in ribbed dark metal, crowned with radomes and cable masts, with yellow service doors.
buildings.entrances: Equipment doors big enough for a truck; staff door by the control room.
buildings.capacity: Radar and sensor coverage of the starboard approaches; a crew of about 20 per shift.
buildings.services: Radio-screened walls, chilled water, duplicate power.
buildings.interior: Array floor (L1): Radar bay 1, radar bay 2, radar bay 3, radar bay 4, radar bay 5, radar bay 6, radar bay 7, radar bay 8, radar bay 9 and 8 more rooms. Gallery floor (L2): Radar bay 1, radar bay 2, radar bay 3, radar bay 4, radar bay 5, radar bay 6, radar bay 7, radar bay 8, radar bay 9 and 4 more rooms.

buildings.name: Gate Traffic Desk
buildings.notes: slots for cruisers using the three gates
buildings.purpose: The desk that books time slots for cruisers using the three Cruiser Gates.
buildings.structure: Concrete frame.
buildings.look: A small purple-trimmed office with a big window facing the cruiser gates.
buildings.entrances: Entrance from the street.
buildings.capacity: About 3,100 staff.
buildings.services: Links to Starboard Approach Control and the Cruiser Gate Control.
buildings.interior: Ground floor (L1): Light court, gate slot desk, gate status board room, reception, toilets, slot office, berth planning room. Office floor 1 to Office floor 2 (L2–L3): Meeting room, tea point, staff toilets and showers, slot office, berth planning room.

buildings.name: Rescue Coordination Centre
buildings.notes: search and rescue (canon Q114) and evacuation flights (canon Q160)
buildings.purpose: The centre that runs search and rescue for Aerion and organises evacuation flights in an emergency.
buildings.structure: Hardened concrete frame with back-up power.
buildings.look: A red-trimmed operations block with a lit red stripe and a rescue-craft pad marked on its roof.
buildings.entrances: Staff entrance; ambulance and equipment entrance at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 4,410 staff over three watches.
buildings.services: Own generators, links to every fire station, hospital and rescue craft.
buildings.interior: Operations floor (L1): Rescue operations room, light court, emergency calls room, rescue craft desk, evacuation planning room, medical liaison desk, kit store, locker room, staff toilets and showers and 1 more rooms. Support floor 1 (L2): Rescue operations room, rest room, mess, training room, staff toilets and showers, offices, exercise planning room. Support floor 2 (L3): Rest room, mess, training room, staff toilets and showers, offices, exercise planning room.

buildings.name: Evacuation Craft Hangar
buildings.purpose: The hangar holding Aerion's evacuation craft, kept ready to fly people out in an emergency.
buildings.structure: Long-span steel hangar, 72 ft (22 m) clear, with fast-opening doors along one side.
buildings.look: A huge steel-grey hangar with a row of tall doors striped orange and white, and readiness lights over each door.
buildings.entrances: A fast-opening door for each craft; staff entrance at the support wing.
buildings.capacity: Aerion's evacuation craft; a standby crew of 1,760.
buildings.services: Fuel lines, power, oxygen and air at every bay; alarm links to the Rescue Coordination Centre.
buildings.interior: Hangar floor (L1): Evacuation craft bay 1, evacuation craft bay 2, evacuation craft bay 3, evacuation craft bay 4, evacuation craft bay 5, evacuation craft bay 6, evacuation craft bay 7, evacuation craft bay 8, boarding hall and 7 more rooms. Gallery floor (L2): Evacuation craft bay 1, evacuation craft bay 2, evacuation craft bay 3, evacuation craft bay 4, evacuation craft bay 5, evacuation craft bay 6, evacuation craft bay 7, evacuation craft bay 8, crew rest rooms and 3 more rooms.

buildings.name: Starboard Controllers' Lodge
buildings.notes: rest rooms for controllers on shift
buildings.purpose: Rest rooms for starboard approach controllers between shifts.
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with heavy sound insulation between rooms.
buildings.look: A quiet starboard lodge in warm tan panels with small deep windows and a walled garden.
buildings.entrances: Front door from the street, a short walk from the control room.
buildings.capacity: About 1,360 rest rooms.
buildings.services: Blackout blinds, wake-up call system, quiet ventilation.
buildings.interior: Lounge floor (L1): Quiet garden, lounge, dining room, kitchen, gym, front desk, toilets, reading room. Rest floor 1 to Rest floor 2 (L2–L3): Rest room, shower room, linen room.

buildings.name: Starboard Approach Utility Plant
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for Starboard Approach, supplying power, air and water.
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete plant hall with fire walls between transformer bays; steel roof trusses carrying a crane rail.
buildings.look: A low ribbed shed with yellow-striped roller doors, a bank of grey transformers behind a mesh fence and pipe bridges running to the street.
buildings.entrances: Wide roller doors for lifting gear on the street side; a crew door with a card reader beside the control room.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling, air and water for every building in Starboard Approach; a crew of about 12 on each shift.
buildings.services: Transformers, switchgear, chillers, air handling, water pumps and treatment, standby batteries; overhead crane.
buildings.interior: Pipe and cable basement (LB1): Cable vault, pipe gallery. Plant floor (L1): Transformer bay 1, transformer bay 2, transformer bay 3, transformer bay 4, transformer bay 5, chiller hall, air handling hall, control room, switch room and 7 more rooms. Upper plant deck (L2): Transformer bay 1, transformer bay 2, transformer bay 3, transformer bay 4, transformer bay 5, chiller hall, air handling hall, filter bank room, ductwork gallery and 2 more rooms.

buildings.name: Starboard Approach Service Shaft
buildings.notes: access to the 60 m service layer
buildings.purpose: The Starboard Approach shaft down to the service layer.
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete shaft, 197 ft (60 m) deep to the service layer, with a steel headframe.
buildings.look: A square tower of ribbed grey panels with a big goods lift door on each side and pipe ducts climbing its walls.
buildings.entrances: Truck door into the loading bay; crew door with card access.
buildings.capacity: Goods lift for loads up to 30 tons; crew lift for 20 people.
buildings.services: Goods and crew lifts, shaft ventilation, gas detection, emergency stair.
buildings.interior: Service layer landing (LB1): Service layer landing, tunnel portal. Lift landing (L1): Shaft and lift landing, lift control room, loading bay, crew check-in, tool store, staff toilets and showers, holding store. Winding room (L2): Shaft and lift landing, winding machinery, shaft ventilation fans, machine gallery.
